_: The ground's look (land3d.gd, terrain.gd read it through data.gd; docs/TUNING.md). The painted look (art-direction/concept-town-repaint.png; Foundation and Tiny Glade's soft painted ground): each layer's tint (multiplies its texture) and scale (texture repeats per game unit: lower is a broader, softer pattern), a wider beach, no surf at the shore. beach.top: how far above the waterline the sand runs (game units; today 0.02). roads: a grass verge either side of each track (verge: its width as a share of the road's; vergeTint: its colour and strength, near the grass's own so it blends, not a yellow band); tint: every road's, street's and track's earth, a multiply on the warm dirt photo (muted and a little cool: it read as a saturated orange stripe); kingsShade: the King's road that much darker; edge: how a track frays into the grass (feather: the soft edge's width as a share of the road's; wander: how far its verges wander in and out; crown: how solid the grassy strip down the middle stays, 1 none; ruts: how dark the two wheel ruts; ends: how far each stretch's ends fray out, as a share of a tile, so the stretches of a street overlap softly instead of ending square, batch 6 (c)). wear (wear.gd): paths worn where people walk (only where they moved at least walkMin units since the last stamp: standing people wear no pads); on, how much a step wears (0..1), how much grows back each upload, how often people are stamped and the wear uploaded (seconds), the bare earth's colour. macro: Terrain3D's broad colour patches over every layer (research #3, the big low-frequency hue tint): two colours (a lush green, a sun-dried yellow), scale the patches' noise (lower is broader; Terrain3D noise1_scale), slope how much slopes take it; set whether the ground is painted or not. painting: which of the painted set's textures the layer draws (Voxel Core Lab Hand-Painted Watercolor Terrain Textures, CC0, Jonas Voland; packed by tools/pack_painted_ground.gd into assets/ground/painted); every layer takes one (tools/ground_check.gd fails a layer that doesn't); lift: how far the painting is washed toward white (the pack has no snow: the snow is its palest stone, lifted). winter.snow: the colour winter's snow lies over the land in (land3d.gd snow_col; was 0.84, 0.86, 0.91: the light pass found the square's blown whites were mostly snow, so about 0.88 of it, its blue cast kept). mesh: Terrain3D's rings of land round the lens (size: vertices across the finest ring, each further ring twice as coarse; lods: how many rings). Its default 48 drew the mid zoom's ground from points 2 units apart, sinking a lake's low shore under the water's surface (the grey smear, fields seen lying on the lake); 128 keeps half-unit detail out to about 30 units. rivers (rivers.gd): never a square end. mouthUnder: how far under the sea's or a lake's surface a river's mouth sinks (game units); mouthEase: over how many of its last points (half a unit apart) it eases down; taper: over how many points a spring's head or a river running into another narrows; thin: how narrow, as a share of its width; shallow, deep: the water's colour (the old peaty 0.2/0.26/0.2 read near black from the mid zoom).

terrain._: The ground by Freeciv's terrain (terrain.gd tile_mix; land3d.gd lays the strongest layer over the grass, blended across tile edges): each terrain's weights of the ground layers in land3d.gd's order: grass, dirt, sand, snow, rock, forest, mud. A river tile (Grassland|river) takes its terrain's. Water tiles are grass here: the beach and the sea floor come from the land's height. patches: worn earth through the grass (Mac, pass 2159: one flat lawn outside the towns; 01-town and 03-army show bare earth and varied ground): layer (its index), most (its weight at a patch's heart, times the tile's grass), from (the noise level where a patch starts: higher, fewer), soft (how far it frays), scale (noise per game unit: higher, smaller patches).
